sources.entry: FileShipper - Peer-to-peer file transfer between computers and phones over local Wi-Fi. ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: FileShipper
summary.one_liner: FileShipper is a local Wi-Fi file transfer tool that moves files between computers (Mac and Windows) and phones directly over the network, without cloud uploads or a phone app.
use_cases: Moving photos and videos from a phone to a computer without cables
Sending files between a Mac and a Windows PC on the same Wi-Fi
Transferring large files over the local network instead of uploading to the cloud
Handing a file to a guest's phone on your Wi-Fi without accounts
Keeping sensitive files off third-party cloud services
summary.what_it_does: FileShipper runs on computers and shows nearby computers and connected phones on an AirDrop-style radar. Tapping a device lets you pick files and send them. Phones do not need an app: they scan a QR code or type an address to open a browser page where they can send files to the computer and download shared files. Transfers go directly between devices over the local network, and the page says nothing is uploaded to a server. Received files go into a folder you choose and are listed under Received Files with a Reveal in Finder or Explorer option. The app can be left open or protected with a PIN, and the address and QR code update when the Wi-Fi network changes.
notable: AirDrop-style radar for choosing nearby devices
Phones connect via QR code and a browser page with no app install
Transfers stay on the local network with no cloud upload
Optional PIN protection and a shared public file pool
caveats: Requires computers and phones to be on the same local Wi-Fi network
Listed as freeware in the awesome-mac list; the page itself does not state a price or license terms
Platform support for Linux and other systems is not mentioned
